posts.title: New feature
posts.content:
Hey, I have a feature idea for Anymex.
It would be a tool to help people who make edits. While watching an anime, users could mark specific timestamps or clip ranges they want to use (for example, from one moment to another).
Then, they could save those clips as visual notes — not just text, but something more organized and aesthetic, with colors, layouts, and maybe thumbnails.
It would basically work like a built-in workspace to plan edits before actually making them.
Also, this wouldn’t require including or redistributing any video content, just saving timestamps and notes, so it should avoid copyright issues.

posts.title: Feature Suggestion: Local Manga/Manhwa Entries
posts.content:
So currently the app depends heavily on AniList/MAL entries for manga pages and tracking. Because of this, series that exist in extensions but not on AniList/MAL (such as TBATE and some webcomics/manhwa) cannot be properly opened or tracked.

It would be great to add support for local entries that users can create manually.

Possible features:
- Create local manga/manhwa pages

- Assign sources/extensions manually

- Save progress locally on-device

This would help support removed, niche, or unsupported series while making extensions much more useful.

posts.title: Feature Request: Improve Discover Section Browsing
posts.content:
I’d like to suggest an improvement for the Discover section in the app. Currently, categories like “Trending Anime” are displayed in a horizontal scroll format, where you can only swipe left and right for a limited number of titles. This makes it difficult to explore more content, especially when trying to find something new to watch.

It would be much better if:

There was an option to expand each category into a full list or grid view

Or allow continuous scrolling (vertical or extended horizontal) to see more titles without hitting a limit

Maybe even add a “See All” button for each category


This would make browsing a lot smoother and help users discover more anime 

Thanks!
